Im sure the question, "Why did you start playing" has been asked, but why did you stick with it?

For me, initially it was to play as fast as possible... but later, it became learning how to PLAY the notes instead of burning through them.

What says you?
Why did you stick with the guitar?

I stuck with it because it was a fun, casual thing for me. I started out on a different instrument, so picking up the guitar was like learning a completely different language. It's a stress relief and it uses a different rhythmic feel and requires separate coordination.
What instrument did you start out on. Do you think it helped you in learning the guitar?

I started on another instrument as well. I joined the school orchestra program in 6th grade on the violin. Eventually I moved around and learned to play all of the stringed instruments offered because I enjoyed the diversity between them. I got into guitar later. I definitely think learning in a structured environment like that helped me out tremendously when I picked up the guitar. My orchestra instructors taught me how to practice, how to read and understand sheet music, and gave me a foundational knowledge of theory that helped me pick out techniques and patterns that came in handy on the guitar.

I picked up the guitar when I was really young, just had one laying around the house and I liked noodling on on it. I quit playing for years but found I'm more content if I'm making up tracks. So I got back into it.

Honest question: How bad did your technique suffer after leaving it for so long? Things like vibrato and dexterity are an example.

Also - POST SOME TRACKS MAN!!! :D

My technique got pretty bad. My fingers were weak and slow. I'm still not where I was in those departments. As annoying as that is, it doesn't matter. It's nothing like starting over from square one though. Muscle memory is amazing. I had an incident and am currently working on getting my picking hand working right, so I don't have any current tracks worth posting. Thanks for showing interest fatty2x4. And if you've got any tracks let me know.

I've stuck with it because I have a goal to be able to play in front of people and be comfortable with it. I'm at the point where I can play a few things in front of people, but I'd only be comfortable with the rest of the band I've been playing with. My real goal is to be confident enough to play solo and even take requests. I'm nearly there.

A goal I have since added is being able to play and sing at the same time.

That said, I'm with /u/bufferoverflow, I'm also able to stick with it because I'm doing it as a hobby, for fun. I'm conscious of not making it a second job.

Awesome comment. I too would love to sing and play at the same time... even talk and play at the same time!

That is one hurdle that I've never been able to get over!

Going to concerts always gets me pumped up when I'm in a rut. Another thing I did was get a very small guitar that I could play anywhere:

http://www.angelfire.com/ca2/smithtone/gi/hohn1.jpg

Also Rocksmith is a great tool for staying motivated and keeping practice fun.

Ultimately, I guess I stuck with it because I am more comfortable with it than any of my other instruments. I have an easier time making music with it. I love playing my other instruments, I'm just not as competent with them. That's really not saying much, as I'm a mediocre guitar player at best. At the end of the day, my goal is to make music, and I can do that most easily with guitar. Huge bonus as a gigging musican: portability.

I started playing drums at the age of 6, by the will of my parents. Somehow then I was playing Piano from the age of 8 till 14 also by the will of my parents. Last year I inherited a classic guitar from a person that I knew since my childhood, she was the mother of my best friend and a music teacher. Guitar was her main instrument. So I said to myself, "I am gonna play this".

So I started to play.

Now I am here.

There has been at least one person in every generation in my family that has played guitar, for as far back as we can remember, so it was sort of inevitable having been exposed to it fro a young age. I knew I always wanted to play it. Admittedly when I first started learning, the fact that I got to skip classes in order to attend music practice was a big factor. Then as I slowly started to get into music more and more, listening to all the old classics and guitar heroes... I wished one day that I could be like them.

What's caused me to stick with it is the satisfaction I get, not just from having a creative outlet to do whatever I need to do, but also that satisfaction you get from learning a new piece you've been stuck on for a long time, or when something finally clicks into place. It feels good, and you want more of it so you keep going. I also love being able to improve so that I can play better with other people - that feeling when you are playing with others and it 'just works' is honestly one of the best feelings ever. Indescribable, just pure euphoria. Lastly I would say that it is one of the few things that has been a constant in my life - other interests and hobbies have come and gone over the years, I have moved around a lot, and friends have begun to move on and start families. Usual stuff for a lot of people, but its been great still having guitar there - at least once thing that has remained constant in my life throughout everything. Feels... comforting.
I so hear you on the euphoric feeling you get when a song comes together with a group! It's like a drug, and the single reason I deal with the hassle of managing a band.

I've never even been part of a proper band, just jam groups. One day I strive to play on a stage with a group, no matter how big or small. Apparently drummers are an endangered species in my town, though.

My advice to you is to start small. Find one key player and form a duo. Grow from there. Shoot, it took me three years, but now I'm fronting a killer Celtic duo on an outer island in Hawaii! You have NO idea how hard it was to find a fiddle player on a low population island in the middle of the Pacific hat was talented and willing to do this type of music!

I've always wanted to be a musician, and guitar is such a versatile instrument. I just loved being able to play pretty much anything I want as long as I put in the time. That, and all the attention I got from girls in high school was a pretty nice perk...

I was really into Avenged Sevenfold during their early and their golden years. Syn was the first guitarist that I really idolized and tried to learn from because his style of playing (melodic & harmonic minor scales, sporadic chromatic elements, and very melodic melodies) was relatively unique to the scene at that time. I loved spending my evenings and weekends learning how to play his solos and trying to learn as much about how he played the way he did. Now I've moved on to other bands (Dream Theater, Between the Buried and Me, Protest The Hero, etc.), but I probably wouldn't have stuck with it without Syn.

I stuck with it because I'd been playing long enough that it would be stupid to quit. I liked knowing more about guitar than the chump trying to woo girls with his mad skillz and I also liked the idea of being a chick with a guitar with mad chops of my own.

Um, also it's fun.

I stuck with it because I felt like I motivated myself to do it unlike other instruments that I was also learning in a class, I also feel like there is a lot more diversity in music with guitars in it just because the sound of the guitar can be altered so much by various things, it seemed sounding pretty much the same all the time was a very boring concept.

I wanted to be the best guitar player I possibly could be! I'm 23 now, started when I was about 8. I don't get to play as much as I use too and try to play as much as possible (still get to each day). I still consider leaving my job and just try and play for a living, but I don't know how that work out... It's not that I don't like my job, but guitar just feels like home and it's one of my most favorite things to do.
I realized early on that I enjoyed the satisfaction of learning a new tune or riff. Now days It's just a part of me that will never go away,

I stuck with it because music is the best thing in my life, I love my guitar, I love my piano. I love making some noice, I love when I try to compose compose something, I love dreaming, I love music :D What can be more beautiful than the music?

It was kind of the same thing, I wanted to learn how to play the notes.

I had an electric guitar that helped me write some crappy punk songs in my younger years, but I had given up on everything at that point. I went through a bad breakup that I couldn't shake.

I saw the movie once, or specifically the song Say It To Me Now by Glen Hansard https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JMqKOt7R_K8 and the whole movie made me want to start writing again, and write from different places that I had before and exploring what these combinations of vocals and notes in a progression helped me work through things and gave me more confidence.

I stuck with guitar cause music stuck with me :D

The fact I could lose myself in something for an hour without realising it.it was casual. When I first got one I spent first few months breathing and eating guitar then slowed to daily to every other day. I got better, people around arevless impressed, so I breathed a little. It's my fun time to play. for me, when I'm sad,happy or bord. I'll hear a song on the radio and if I can play it its the first thing I do when I get home. If not I'll try and learn it or just the part that I like or can easily play.

That's why I stuck with it. Its a skill I built over time and I can craft my emotions or emulate others with my favorite tool.
